name: Lance Martin
bio: Member of technical staff at Anthropic. Working on the Claude Platform, including Claude Managed Agents and the claude-api skill in Claude Code. Prior to Anthropic, was one of the early team at LangChain. Prior to LangChain, spent several years focused on vision for self-driving cars (Uber ATG, Ike, Nuro) and got a PhD from Stanford.

positions.claim: Async agent experiences are only viable once model task horizons exceed roughly an hour; below that, the agent errors out and returns too quickly for async to be a good UX.
Putting the harness and the sandbox in the same container is the wrong architecture for long-horizon agents, because a container death loses the entire session.
Credentials should live in a separate vault and never be added to the agent's sandbox container.
An append-only, immutable session log is superior to destructive compaction because the model can always fetch back old context.
Self-grading in the same context window that produced the work causes confabulation and odd artifacts; verification must be a separate, separately tuned context.
Build/verifier loops paired with high-capacity models are a good general primitive for long-running asynchronous work.
Claude's in-band memory writing has improved measurably across model generations, from Sonnet 3.5 to 4.6, on both Pokémon progress and Continual Learning Bench.
The key capability difference between low- and high-capacity models at memory writing is distillation — knowing which generalizable abstraction to save rather than which specific fact.
In-band memory writing alone is insufficient; an out-of-band consolidation pass is required to correct incorrect or only-locally-optimal memories.
Frontier models operate in a 12+ hour task horizon regime on METR, including OpenAI's Codex, while non-frontier models do not.
The frontier gap in long-horizon agent products comes from combined investment in architecture, infrastructure, security, and memory — not model capability alone.
The choice between file system and database as a memory substrate does not matter much; what matters is that the substrate is highly programmable with simple primitives.
Prescriptive memory schemas that pre-specify what types of memories to save cause performance to drop relative to letting the model manage memory freely.
Agent harnesses will shift from single-player and reactive to multiplayer, org-scoped, and proactive.
Dreaming's offline compute cost needs to be justified with evals in your own context rather than assumed worthwhile.
